title: A content-addressed snapshot store in S3

blocks.text: The planning service is moving its snapshots from a worker's disk to S3, so that every worker, and every auditor, reads the same inputs. Your milestone writes the store: each snapshot is kept once under its own content hash and checked again whenever it is read. The tests run against moto's in-memory S3 with moto's fake credentials: no account, no network. The practice portfolio is invented for a fictional utility.

A snapshot is a dict in the milestones' shape (`years`, `rate`, `budget`, `region_budget`, `crews`, `floor`, `projects`), with integer year keys in `budget`, in each region's `region_budget`, in each program's `crews` and in each project's `npv`. JSON can only write text keys, so the years come out of S3 as strings.

rows: `json.dumps` with sorted keys, no spaces, ASCII only, as bytes
the snapshot back from those bytes, with every year key listed above an `int` again

the digest is the SHA-256 hex digest of the canonical bytes, and the key is `snapshots/<digest>.json`. Ask `head_object` first; call `put_object` only when nothing is stored under the key. Return the digest

raise `NotStored` if no object has that key (a `head_object` that answers 404 raises botocore's `ClientError`, whose `response["Error"]["Code"]` is `"404"`); read the object, re-hash its bytes, raise `Corrupted` if they no longer hash to the digest, otherwise return `from_json` of them

blocks.text: Lessons 12.5.3 and 12.5.4 cover the services; the S3 calls you need are `head_object`, `put_object` and `get_object(...)["Body"].read()`, each with `Bucket=` and `Key=`. About thirty lines.

Each snapshot is stored once, as `snapshots/<sha256>.json`, and checked again on every read. A

"""

cases.says: a snapshot is stored as snapshots/<digest>.json, the digest is the SHA-256 of its canonical bytes, and it reads back
storing equal content again finds the object and writes nothing
the same snapshot built in another key order has the same bytes
an object changed after it was stored is refused on the next read
year keys, which JSON turns into text, are integers again at every level after a read
reading a digest that was never stored raises the store's own error, not botocore's
